name: date-range-picker
purpose: A time range for queries over time: logs, events, traces and metrics. After the Console Kit date-time range (quick ranges, a custom duration, absolute range with times, a range that ends now, previous and next, auto refresh, the time zone) and Cloudscape's date range picker. The value is one of three shapes: - **relative** — `{ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute' }`, read as "the last 15 minutes" and re-resolved against the clock on every query, so a live view keeps moving. With `snap: true` the start is rounded down to the start of the unit in the time zone: `{ amount: 1, unit: 'day', snap: true }` is **Today** (midnight to now), `unit: 'week'` is **This week** (from Sunday, like the month grid). - **absolute** — `{ type: 'absolute', start, end }`, two ISO 8601 instants. - **since** — `{ type: 'since', start }`, an ISO 8601 start and an end that is always now ("from the incident until now"). The trigger prints `Last 15 minutes`, `Today`, the absolute range in the selected time zone with its UTC offset (`Nov 10, 16:00 – 17:00 (UTC+00:00)`; the date is printed once when both ends are on the same day), or `Nov 10, 2026, 9:30 – now`. It never cuts the text off: a long value wraps onto a second line. The panel switches between Relative (first) and Absolute. Absolute shows the `DatePicker` month grid **first** (click a start day and an end day; its caption has Month and Year selects between the previous and next month arrows), then the start and end date and time fields that the grid fills in and that can also be typed (each time field a `Combobox` that takes a typed time or lists the day in 30-minute steps, plus the current time when it falls between two, opened under the field and scrolled to the current time; the times are hidden with `showTime` off), then, when the picker also offers relative ranges, an **End at now** switch that makes a `since` range. Relative shows the quick ranges first, two columns when there is room (read down the first column, then the second), then one **Custom range** row; choosing it replaces the quick ranges with the Duration and Unit fields and a **Back to quick ranges** button, so the form stays out of the way until someone asks for it (the CloudWatch pattern: quick picks first, a custom duration one click away). The default quick ranges are Today, This week, Last minute, Last 5, 15 and 30 minutes, Last hour, Last 24 hours, Last 7, 30 and 90 days and Last year; `relativeOptions` replaces them. The panel opens on Relative unless the committed value is absolute or `since` (then Absolute). The panel does not name the time zone: the page states it beside the picker, always visible (`Times in UTC` or a Time zone select in the toolbar, see `blocks/view/events-explorer`), and the trigger of an absolute range carries its UTC offset. With `showTimeZone` the panel shows the time zone selector above Apply (a `Combobox`: type a city or a zone to filter the list), for a page that has no toolbar of its own to hold it. Above it a **Refresh every** select (Off, 10 seconds … 1 hour; **5 minutes** by default) sets the auto-refresh interval whenever the panel offers relative ranges (`showRefresh` turns it off). Every select in the panel (Unit, Refresh every, the calendar's Month and Year) is the WebKit `Select`, never a native `select`. The panel commits only on Apply; Cancel and Escape drop the draft. Absolute boundaries are typed as wall-clock time in the selected zone and stored as instants, so the same value reads correctly in every zone. With `showStep`, Previous and Next move the range by its own length. On a phone (below 640 px) the panel is a full-width sheet at the bottom of the screen. Every range stays inside limits the page can set: `min` (unset: the start of the day five years ago), `max` (unset: the end of today; a later date allows future dates, for a maintenance window or an alert schedule) and `maxDuration` (unset: any length). They disable the days, months and years outside them in the calendar, drop the quick ranges that do not fit, and refuse a typed range or a custom duration that does not fit with a message. Date math uses `Intl` and the native `Date` only.
useWhen: Use DateRangePicker for any start–end range: relative ('last 24 hours') or absolute, with or without times; turn times off for whole-day reports and billing periods. For one date use DatePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
Filtering events, logs, traces or metrics by time, where "the last N minutes" must stay relative.
Any range that needs times of day and a time zone, not only dates.
Investigations that page through time window by window (`show-step`).
Whole-day ranges for a report or a billing period: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with `:show-time="false"`.

Dashboards and live logs that re-run their query on a timer (`v-model:refresh-interval`, `@refresh`). Auto refresh is **on by default** (every 5 minutes), so every page must handle `@refresh` by re-running its query; a page that cannot re-run it passes `:show-refresh="false"` (or binds `v-model:refresh-interval` to `0` to start with it off).
avoidWhen: A single date or a date and time → use `date-picker`.
A fixed list of named intervals and nothing custom → use `select` or `toggle-group`.
related: `date-picker` — the month grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector come from its internal parts, so both pickers look and behave the same. Split: DatePicker picks one date (optionally with a time); DateRangePicker owns every range and keeps a relative window relative.
`timestamp` — displays a moment in time; both read the `ConfigProvider` `timeZone`.
`config-provider` — its `timeZone` is the zone the picker formats in while `v-model:time-zone` is unbound.
`field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
`property-filter` — the query bar it sits next to in an events toolbar.
`chart` — the histogram whose brush usually writes an absolute range back into this picker.
bestPractices: Keep relative and `since` values relative: resolve them to instants when the query runs (`now - amount × unit` to `now`, or `start` to `now`), never when the user picks them. `useTimeRange(value, { timeZone })` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-time-range` returns `from` and `to`, rounds `snap` ranges in the zone, and holds the window until `refresh()`; call that `refresh()` from `@refresh`. Its `TIME_RANGE_PRESETS` (last hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days) go in `relative-options`.

Fix the reference clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages so labels and step limits are deterministic: `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` covers every picker below it; the `now` prop overrides it for one picker.
Bind `v-model:time-zone` to the user's saved preference, and show times elsewhere on the page in the same zone.

Set `min` to the retention limit and `maxDuration` to the longest window the query can answer, instead of validating after Apply. The defaults (five years back to the end of today) suit logs and metrics; pass a later `max` only where a future range makes sense (a maintenance window, an alert schedule).

State the time zone on the page, beside the picker and always visible (`Times in UTC`, or a Time zone `Select` when the person can change it), on every page that shows metrics and logs; the picker panel does not repeat it.
Name the picker after what it filters (`aria-label="Events time range"`).
Always handle `@refresh`: the picker refreshes every 5 minutes unless the page turns it off, so a page that ignores the event offers a refresh that does nothing.

props.name: relativeOptions
props.doc: Quick ranges listed on the Relative tab.

props.name: timeZones
props.doc: Zones offered by the selector. Empty falls back to the zones `Intl` supports.

props.name: showTimeZone
props.doc: Shows the time zone selector in the panel. Off, the panel says nothing about the zone and the page states it.

props.name: showTime
props.doc: Shows the start and end time fields of an absolute range. Off, a range covers whole days (a report or billing period).

props.name: showStep
props.doc: Shows Previous and Next buttons that move the range back or forward by its own length.

props.name: showRefresh
props.doc: Shows the Refresh every selector in the panel while it offers relative ranges; bind v-model:refresh-interval and run the query on refresh.

props.name: rangeSelectorMode
props.doc: Which kinds of range the panel offers.

props.name: min
props.default: undefined (the start of the day five years before today)
props.doc: Earliest selectable instant. Unset, the start of the day five years before today.

props.name: max
props.doc: Latest selectable instant. Unset, the end of today; pass a later date to allow future dates.

props.name: maxDuration
props.doc: Longest range a person may pick, for example 90 days. Unset, any length between min and max.

props.name: now
props.doc: Reference clock for relative ranges and stepping. Unset uses the nearest `ConfigProvider`'s `now`, then the real clock.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Trigger text with no range. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the trigger. Empty uses the Field label inside a `Field`, else the locale catalog.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the trigger and the step buttons.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the trigger invalid: sets `aria-invalid` and the danger border. An enclosing `Field`'s `invalid` sets it too.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled (`v-model:open` unbound).

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token of the trigger and the panel controls.

props.name: customRangeDisplay
props.doc: Proposal, owner to pick: a Custom range row that opens a form, a link under the quick ranges that opens it, or the duration and unit always shown inline.

props.name: absoluteLayout
props.doc: Proposal, owner to pick: today's stacked Absolute tab, a compact one, the fields first with the calendar on demand, or the fields beside the calendar.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model`).

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:timeZone`).

props.name: open
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:open`).

props.name: refreshInterval
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:refreshInterval`).

events.name: refresh
events.notes: On every auto-refresh tick while `refreshInterval` is above 0 (5 minutes by default), Refresh every is offered, the picker is enabled and the page is visible. A timer signal, not a user action: it carries no DOM event.
